problem: "The name marks the short-wavelength end of the spectrum; the divergence appears even earlier, in the far ultraviolet and X-rays." The word "earlier" is ambiguous (earlier in wavelength? earlier in time?) and reads as if the divergence happens somewhere other than at short λ. A student can take it to mean the Rayleigh-Jeans formula stops diverging beyond the ultraviolet.
fix: Replace with: "The name marks the short-wavelength end of the spectrum, but the divergence is not limited to the ultraviolet: the predicted intensity keeps growing without limit through the X-ray and gamma-ray region as well."

where: Section 3, first paragraph and Planck formula, plus quiz Q8 answer
problem: The exponent is not marked up in running text: "hν ÷ (ehν/kT − 1)", "ehν/kT ≈ 1 + hν/kT" and "hν e−hν/kT" read as e times hν/kT, not e raised to the power hν/kT. On a phone this is the most misread line in the chapter. The displayed formula uses <sup> correctly; the prose and the quiz answer do not.
fix: Use the sup tag everywhere: "hν ÷ (e<sup>hν/kT</sup> − 1)", "e<sup>hν/kT</sup> ≈ 1 + hν/kT", "hν e<sup>−hν/kT</sup>".

where: Section 3, Planck's radiation law formula note
problem: The symbol I was defined in Section 1 as power per unit area per unit wavelength (W·m⁻² per m), and the prefactor 2πhc²/λ⁵ is correct for that quantity. The note then calls I "spectral radiance per unit wavelength". Radiance is power per unit area per unit solid angle per unit wavelength, and for radiance the prefactor is 2hc²/λ⁵, without the π. A student who compares with a textbook that uses B_λ will find a factor π that is not explained.
fix: Call I "the spectral exitance (power emitted per unit area per unit wavelength)" and keep 2πhc²/λ⁵, or keep the word radiance and change the prefactor to 2hc²/λ⁵. Do not use both the area-normalised definition and the word radiance.
